title: Rightsizing: pay for what you actually use

kcs.statement: Rightsizing is matching instance types and sizes to a workload's measured performance and capacity needs at the lowest cost, for example moving a server that averages 10% CPU to a smaller size.
Rightsizing is an ongoing process based on utilisation data, and it should happen before committing to long-term discounts, because the cloud lets you change size at any time.

problem_ideas: An instance at $0.40/hour averages 8% CPU; halving its size halves the price: compute the yearly saving.
